messages:
acme-customer: Hey team — running into streaming truncation from Redwood API. Client gets partial SSE payload then connection reset after ~20-30s. Happens consistently when routing through our Envoy ingress. Direct-to-service (bypassing Envoy) works fine. Repro: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream\"` — after ~25s curl prints last chunk and then: 

Maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting that — we'll help debug. Quick Qs: is Envoy terminating TLS or passing through? Any cloud LB before Envoy (ALB/Cloudflare)? Do you have request id / response headers from the failed request?

acme-customer: Envoy terminates TLS on-cluster (http/1.1 to upstream). No ALB in front. We see Envoy log lines at the same time: `upstream read error: EOF` and `connection closed before end_stream`. No obvious Redwood request-id in the log though. Case ID 12345.

Maya (Support): Two usual culprits: (1) proxy/ALB idle timeouts or connection resets (2) response buffering or HTTP/1.1 proxy behaviors that collapse chunks. Since direct-to-service works, likely Envoy config. Can you paste the listener/cluster http protocol options?

acme-customer: Here's a trimmed snippet of our Envoy cluster config (sensitive bits removed):

```yaml
clusters:
  - name: redwood-upstream
    connect_timeout: 5s
    type: STRICT_DNS
    lb_policy: ROUND_ROBIN
    http_protocol_options:
      idle_timeout: 30s
    upstream_connection_options:
      tcp_keepalive:
        keepalive_time: 60
```

acme-customer: We set idle_timeout to 30s because of other shorter requests — maybe that's the problem?

Kevin (Eng Runtime): That idle_timeout looks suspicious. For SSE/long polling you need stream idle timeout or no idle timeout so server-originated silence doesn't close the connection. Envoy has a couple of knobs: `idle_timeout` on the upstream cluster, and `stream_idle_timeout` on the HTTP connection manager (or per-route). If set to 30s, Envoy will close after 30s of no requests/bytes upstream. If your LLM backend sends tokens less frequently than that (or you don't flush small chunks), Envoy can tear it down with an upstream EOF.

Kevin (Eng Runtime): Also check `disable_chunked_encoding`/response buffer config. Envoy can buffer entire responses for certain filters — ensure `proxy_buffering` equivalent is off. For HTTP/1.1 SSE make sure Transfer-Encoding: chunked is preserved and server flushes.

Lisa (SRE): Quick notes: ALB default idle timeout is 60s; NLB is different. If you were in front of a cloud LB, that could explain 60s cutoffs. Envoy side, if you have an HTTP connection manager filter, search for `stream_idle_timeout` or `common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout`. If you want to keep things simple while debugging, temporarily set idle timeout to 0 (disabled) or a generous value like 5m to see if truncation stops.

Maya (Support): Practical repro steps you can run now (low-friction):
1) Bypass Envoy (port-forward or temporary k8s svc to pod) and run the curl `-N` test — you said this works already, that's a good baseline.
2) Curl to Envoy with verbose and show headers: `curl -v -N --http1.1 -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://<envoy>/v1/stream` — capture full curl output (request/response headers + timing).
3) On Envoy pod: `kubectl logs -c envoy <pod> --since=10m` around the timestamp. Also capture `tcpdump -i any port 443 -w /tmp/stream.pcap` for one repro (if you can share).
4) Temporarily set `idle_timeout: 0s` or increase to 5m in cluster/listener and redeploy. See if truncation stops.

acme-customer: Will run the verbose curl and pick logs. One question — we currently don't send interim heartbeat comments from the app. Would sending `: keepalive\n\n` every 10s be a reasonable workaround?

Kevin (Eng Runtime): Yes, heartbeat comments (SSE comment `: ping\n\n`) are a reliable workaround because they produce bytes and keep the connection active across proxies that only look at byte activity. But it's a workaround — root fix is to adjust proxy idle timeouts or stream idle settings. Also ensure your application flushes after every chunk (some frameworks buffer until buffer full).

Maya (Support): For Envoy config example (try adding or changing these):
```yaml
http_connection_manager:
  name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
  typed_config:
    \"@type\": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
    stream_idle_timeout: 0s  # disable stream idle timeout while testing
    use_remote_address: true
    # make sure buffers/filters don't buffer the response
    normalize_path: true
```

Maya (Support): And for cluster-level idle timeout make it explicit: `common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout: 0s` or `5m` depending on policy.

ops-bot: Note: Case 12345 assigned to Kevin (Eng Runtime) — escalation level: high — created incident link: https://redwood.incidents/RC-12345

Kevin (Eng Runtime): I'll pull the trace for the request ids you collect and check for upstream resets. If you can share tcpdump or curl -v output, drop it here (sensitive tokens masked). Also note whether you're doing HTTP/1.1 keepalive vs h2 — HTTP/2 has different flow and timeouts.

acme-customer: Thanks — running tests now. If increases to idle_timeout 0s stop the truncation, we'll stage a more conservative change and add SSE pings from our service. Will paste logs shortly.

Maya (Support): Great — ping us when you have logs. If truncation persists even with idle_timeout disabled, we'll wire up a short repro in our staging to reproduce and escalate deeper. :thumbsup:
